title: The time derivative, rewritten
spoken: The time derivative is gamma times the primed time derivative minus v times the primed x derivative.
explanation: The rate of change with stationary time, written through the moving system's derivatives. Per second on both sides.
assumptions: The moving system moves along x at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c. Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, c its V.
Partial derivatives of a field, taken in each system's own coordinates; the chain rule through the Lorentz transformation relates them.

notes.title: The two together
notes.explanation: The chain rule: a change in one stationary coordinate moves both moving coordinates.

notes.title: The matching rate in the moving system
notes.explanation: The same kind of derivative, in the moving system's coordinates.

notes.title: Rate of change in the stationary system
notes.explanation: How a field changes with this stationary-system coordinate, the others held fixed.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: An identity between operators: it holds for any field it is applied to. Substituted into both of Maxwell's equations for a plane wave, it regroups them into the same equations for the primed fields.

notes.title: Times gamma
notes.explanation: The same factor as the transformation itself.

notes.title: The other rate in the moving system
notes.explanation: Because each moving coordinate depends on both x and t, the other derivative enters too.

notes.title: Times v
notes.explanation: How strongly the other coordinate enters.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared. At 0.6c it is 1.25.

notes.title: Time, stationary system
notes.explanation: t: the derivative is taken as t varies.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: Along x. Its sign gives the direction.
